key_insight: A probabilistic deep-learning model can forecast Alzheimer’s disease progression over multiple future visits while quantifying how uncertain each prediction is.
clinical_relevance: This may help researchers better understand who is likely to progress from MCI to dementia and how reliable those forecasts are, but it is not a standalone clinical decision tool.
method: Temporal Fusion Transformer encoder with CORAL ordinal diagnosis output
Autoregressive Mixture Density Network for 5-year trajectories of diagnosis, CDR-SB, MMSE orientation, and hippocampal volume
Aleatoric vs epistemic uncertainty estimated with mixture variance and a 5-member bootstrap ensemble
evidence_signal: On ADNI, the model outperformed linear, recurrent, and transformer baselines for next-visit diagnosis prediction, and external testing on OASIS-3 showed higher epistemic uncertainty alongside larger prediction error.
watch_item: Performance may be less stable for rare progression patterns and external populations, so prospective validation is needed before any real-world use.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Longitudinal Forecasting of Alzheimer's Disease Progression Using Deep Learning
